rows.title: Forward and Reverse Finite Path-Law Ratio

maturity_record.invariant: A finite forward path law is reconstructed pointwise from its supported reverse-aligned law and likelihood ratio, while both path laws normalize and path reversal is involutive.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The path carrier is finite and reverse-aligned mass must be strictly positive for the ratio reconstruction. FinitePathProtocol stores normalized laws and an involution; it does not derive reversal or reverse dynamics from a microscopic process.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Unequal full-support forward and reverse-aligned laws yield nonunit path ratios, while an involution with a two-path swap exercises a genuine reversal.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep093_forward_reverse_pathLaw_ratio:
theorem fep093_forward_reverse_pathLaw_ratio
    (protocol : FinitePathProtocol Path)
    (hReverse : ∀ path, 0 < protocol.reverseAligned path) (path : Path) :
    pathRatio protocol path * protocol.reverseAligned path =
      protocol.forward path
qualified_declaration_statements.fep093_pathLaws_normalized:
theorem fep093_pathLaws_normalized
    (protocol : FinitePathProtocol Path) :
    (∑ path, protocol.forward path = 1) ∧
      ∑ path, protocol.reverseAligned path = 1
qualified_declaration_statements.fep093_pathReversal_involutive:
theorem fep093_pathReversal_involutive
    (protocol : FinitePathProtocol Path) (path : Path) :
    protocol.reversal (protocol.reversal path) = path

rows.statement_review: A supported denominator reconstructs forward mass by division cancellation; normalization and involution are explicit carrier fields. Forward support is not needed for this primary identity. The reversal need not exchange laws.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: FinitePathProtocol by itself supplies two arbitrary normalized laws and an independent involution. Actual homogeneous Markov path masses, normalized laws, finite reversal and endpoint marginal identities are already implemented in path_thermodynamics; do not label them absent. No continuous-path existence or microscopic reverse-process identification follows.

rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: Identity reversal and unequal laws are permitted; this does not imply exchange or entropy-production antisymmetry. At zero reverse mass the totalized ratio is0 and reconstructing positive forward mass fails.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 010 is native reversible-kernel stationarity;025 oriented currents. The093 relation pairs the finite ratio with native identity reversibility, not an equivalence of dynamic carriers.

maturity_record.assumption_review: The primary equality is the maintained definition of entropyProduction. Expected-log-ratio expansion requires strict support of both path laws, and the project's totalized real KL is not an extended divergence at zero reverse mass.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The compiled irreversible Boolean protocol has unequal full-support path laws and therefore supplies positive, rather than merely nonnegative, production in the later dissipation topic.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep094_entropyProduction_as_pathKL:
theorem fep094_entropyProduction_as_pathKL
    (protocol : FinitePathProtocol Path) :
    entropyProduction protocol =
      finiteKL protocol.forward protocol.reverseAligned

theorem fep094_entropyProduction_expected_logRatio
    (protocol : FinitePathProtocol Path)
    (hForward : ∀ path, 0 < protocol.forward path)
    (hReverse : ∀ path, 0 < protocol.reverseAligned path) :
    entropyProduction protocol =
      ∑ path, protocol.forward path * pathwiseEntropyProduction protocol path
qualified_declaration_statements.fep094_entropyProduction_nonnegative:
theorem fep094_entropyProduction_nonnegative
    (protocol : FinitePathProtocol Path) :
    0 ≤ entropyProduction protocol

rows.title: Detailed Fluctuation Symmetry

maturity_record.invariant: Under full path support, reverse-aligned mass times exponential pointwise entropy production reconstructs forward mass, and an exchanging reversal makes entropy production antisymmetric.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Forward and reverse-aligned laws are strictly positive. Antisymmetry further assumes that the recorded involution exchanges the two aligned laws in both directions; these exchange laws are not derived from protocol dynamics.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: A two-path protocol with swapped unequal full-support masses has nonzero pointwise entropy production whose sign reverses on the paired path.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: native Lean compile of fep095_detailedFluctuation_symmetry and fep095_entropyProduction_reversal_antisymmetry with both exchange hypotheses.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep095_detailedFluctuation_symmetry:
theorem fep095_detailedFluctuation_symmetry
    (protocol : FinitePathProtocol Path)
    (hForward : ∀ path, 0 < protocol.forward path)
    (hReverse : ∀ path, 0 < protocol.reverseAligned path) (path : Path) :
    protocol.reverseAligned path *
        Real.exp (pathwiseEntropyProduction protocol path) =
      protocol.forward path
qualified_declaration_statements.fep095_entropyProduction_reversal_antisy:
theorem fep095_entropyProduction_reversal_antisymmetry
    (protocol : FinitePathProtocol Path)
    (hForward : ∀ path, 0 < protocol.forward path)
    (hReverse : ∀ path, 0 < protocol.reverseAligned path)
    (hExchangeForward : ∀ path,
      protocol.forward (protocol.reversal path) = protocol.reverseAligned path)
    (hExchangeReverse : ∀ path,
      protocol.reverseAligned (protocol.reversal path) = protocol.forward path)
    (path : Path) :
    pathwiseEntropyProduction protocol (protocol.reversal path) =
      -pathwiseEntropyProduction protocol path

rows.statement_review: For positive forward/reverse masses, exp(log ratio) reconstructs the forward mass. Reversal antisymmetry further requires both exchange laws; involution alone is insufficient.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: The main identity is likelihood-ratio algebra, not a derived law of microscopic reversibility. The stored irreversibleBoolProtocol has identity reversal and unequal laws; it proves positive production but does not satisfy the exchange hypotheses. A separate swapped-law protocol can.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: Use forward true3/4,false1/4, reverse masses swapped and Bool.not reversal; sigma(true)=log3 and sigma(false)=-log3.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: Take the same unequal masses with identity reversal: sigma at a point is nonzero and does not become its negative on reversal.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 093 adds ratio reconstruction without forward positivity;095 adds supported exponential identity and optional exchange-specific antisymmetry. Native010 stationarity is only paired, not used to derive exchange.

novelty_record.new_invariant: Reverse path mass times exponential entropy production reconstructs forward mass and reverses sign under exchange.
novelty_record.carrier_delta: Adds full-support aligned path laws plus an involution that explicitly exchanges forward and reverse probabilities.

touching_relations.rationale: Detailed finite fluctuation symmetry and native kernel reversibility each recover their corresponding forward or invariant law.

maturity_record.assumption_review: The path carrier is finite and both path laws have strict support, so the likelihood ratio and logarithm are ordinary real values. The theorem does not treat singular path measures or continuous-time trajectories.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Unequal full-support path laws produce nonconstant entropy-production values whose weighted exponentials still normalize exactly to one.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep096_integralFluctuation_theorem:

    (protocol : FinitePathProtocol Path)
    (hForward : ∀ path, 0 < protocol.forward path)
    (hReverse : ∀ path, 0 < protocol.reverseAligned path) :
    ∑ path, protocol.forward path *
        Real.exp (-pathwiseEntropyProduction protocol path) = 1

rows.statement_review: Finite forward expectation of exp(-log(forward/reverse)) is reverse-law total mass1. Both strict-support hypotheses are explicit and sufficient; reversal does not enter the proof.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: This is a normalized finite change-of-measure identity, not singular-path or continuous-time stochastic-process existence. Full support is stronger than necessary but cannot be silently removed from the current theorem.

rows.title: Finite Jarzynski Equality

maturity_record.invariant: A normalized finite exponential-work protocol has work average equal to the exponential of negative inverse temperature times free-energy difference.
maturity_record.assumption_review: HasJarzynskiNormalization explicitly packages positive beta and the identity that the expectation of exp(-beta times (work minus free-energy difference)) equals one. The theorem algebraically extracts Jarzynski's equality from this normalization; it does not derive that premise from microscopic reversibility.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Nonconstant finite work values can satisfy the normalization after choosing a compatible free-energy difference, while beta positivity excludes the zero-temperature-parameter collapse.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: native Lean compile of fep097_finiteJarzynski_equality with the explicit beta, work, free-energy, and normalization certificate.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep097_finiteJarzynski_equality:
theorem fep097_finiteJarzynski_equality
    (law : FiniteLaw Path) (beta deltaFreeEnergy : ℝ)
    (work : Path → ℝ)
    (hNormalization :
      HasJarzynskiNormalization law beta deltaFreeEnergy work) :
    exponentialWorkAverage law beta work =
      Real.exp (-beta * deltaFreeEnergy)

rows.statement_review: The primary extracts exponentialWorkAverage=exp(-beta*deltaF) from an explicitly assumed normalization with beta>0. This is accurately conditional_proxy, not a derivation of that physical premise.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: The foundation already derives normalization and Jarzynski from the per-path HasCrooksRelation, constructs a nonconstant Boolean work witness and proves normalization without Crooks is possible. Defining work=deltaF+sigma/beta supplies a formal Crooks instance but does not identify mechanical work. Beta has inverse-energy meaning only with explicit unit convention; beta0 is zero inverse temperature, conventionally an infinite-temperature limit, not zero temperature.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: Reuse irreversibleBool_crooks at beta1,deltaF0 and work ±log3, then finiteJarzynski_of_crooks.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: Reuse jarzynski_without_crooks (zero work normalizes but fails pathwise relation) and irreversibleForward_unitWork_not_jarzynski. Do not assume arbitrary supplied work satisfies normalization.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 013 algebraic Helmholtz difference and097 exponential work remain separate in the bridge; no equality of deltaF with that Helmholtz difference is proved.

novelty_record.new_invariant: Explicit finite exponential-work normalization implies the Jarzynski work–free-energy equality.
novelty_record.carrier_delta: Adds positive inverse temperature, a path work observable, free-energy difference, and a named normalization certificate.

touching_relations.rationale: The finite Jarzynski normalization and the original Helmholtz difference identity are retained as separate assumptions, avoiding a microscopic-energy identification that neither theorem proves.

rows.title: Reversible-Chain One-Step KL Dissipation

maturity_record.invariant: One strictly positive reversible finite Markov step cannot increase KL to its stationary law; the identity transition saturates equality and an explicit irreversible path protocol has positive entropy production.
maturity_record.assumption_review: State is finite and nonempty, actual and stationary laws have full support, every transition atom is positive, and detailed balance supplies stationarity. The result is one-step dissipation, not strict contraction for every nonidentity kernel or a continuous-time entropy-production theorem.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The identity kernel proves the exact reversible equality boundary, while the unequal full-support Boolean path witness proves strictly positive production away from reversibility.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: native Lean compile of fep099_reversibleChain_oneStep_KL_dissipation, fep099_reversibleEquality_boundary, and fep099_irreversiblePositiveProduction_witness.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep099_reversibleChain_oneStep_KL_dissip:
theorem fep099_reversibleChain_oneStep_KL_dissipation
    [Nonempty State]
    (actual stationary : FiniteLaw State)
    (kernel : FiniteKernel State State)
    (hActual : ∀ state, 0 < actual state)
    (hStationary : ∀ state, 0 < stationary state)
    (hKernel : ∀ source target, 0 < kernel source target)
    (hReversible : IsReversible stationary kernel) :
    finiteKL (kernel.predictive actual) stationary ≤
      finiteKL actual stationary
qualified_declaration_statements.fep099_reversibleEquality_boundary:
theorem fep099_reversibleEquality_boundary [DecidableEq State]
    (actual stationary : FiniteLaw State) :
    finiteKL
        ((FiniteKernel.identity : FiniteKernel State State).predictive actual)
        stationary = finiteKL actual stationary

rows.statement_review: Full-support finite-channel DPI plus detailed-balance stationarity proves a one-step KL nonincrease. The identity equality theorem is separate and imposes no strict transition support. A distinct supplied unequal path-law witness has positive production.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: On a state space with at least2 elements identity has zero off-diagonal entries and does not instantiate hKernel. Positive path production alone does not certify a nonreversible transition process; the separate biasedCycleKernel supplies that stronger finite-chain witness. Existing entropyProduction_markov_reversible_KL_drop and composed one-step reduction identify actual path production with endpoint KL loss at every supported finite horizon.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: Use a strictly positive symmetric Boolean mixing kernel with stationary uniform and nonuniform positive actual law; compare one-step KL. For actual nonreversibility reuse biasedCycle_not_reversible and horizon-positive production.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: Identity equality lies outside the main theorem support class for multi-state spaces. At actual=stationary even a strictly positive nonidentity kernel has equality, so nonidentity alone does not yield strict dissipation.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 010 provides stationarity;014 nativeKL. The original composition is a conjunction, whereas the separate fep099_markov_path_KL_drop_reduction is a genuine same-carrier reduction. No strict contraction, rate or infinite-time entropy result is claimed.
